style: Read clearly and naturally, at a moderate pace
lines: Welcome to Rollercoaster Polynomials. Drag the footings along the ground, and the track bends to fit them.
Each footing is a zero of the polynomial. The leftmost and rightmost zeros are your stations.
Multiplicity one crosses the ground. Two touches and turns back. Three crosses flat.
Odd degree ends point opposite ways. Even degree ends point the same way.
The leading coefficient sets how tall the track is. Flip it, and hills become tunnels.
Survey mode. The office sent a plan in standard form. Plant a stake to find out how high the track is there.
The remainder of dividing by x minus c is the height of the track at c.
Remainder zero. So x minus c is a factor, and a footing goes here.
Not a double footing. The remaining part is not zero here.
The remaining part never reaches zero for a real number, so the track never touches the ground again.
Every footing found. Factored form and standard form describe the same track.
Commissions. Each order lists what the park wants. Build a track that meets every line.
Match the ghost track. Read its zeros and how it meets the ground, then set the height.
